SystemSketch · deep research dictionary · 04 September 2026

LabVIEW, Unreal Blueprint & Simulink
Vocabulary and UI Controls Gap Analysis

A concept-by-concept evidence dictionary, now including the application chrome outside the canvas: menus, toolbars, run controls, inspectors, tabs, navigators, search, diagnostics, bookmarks, and debugging surfaces.

How to read a useful row

Every useful entry follows the requested order: plain-language description, real official-documentation screenshots side by side, then an original SystemSketch proposal and honest implementation lift.

The source-authority filter

Borrow controls that reveal a Python, board, run, or trace fact. Reject controls that would make the canvas a second program, schema, simulator, asset database, or deployment system.

Corrected conclusion

More already exists; the remaining gaps are specific

Split, required/default/override readability, variadic groups, the Inspector, Problems, command search, library, Board Overview, depth navigation, comments, and layout commands are already real SystemSketch UI—not proposals.

What changed after Zach's review: Split moved to Already have. Set attributes and Select are approved stock-block directions. Error, event, state, and configuration remain ordinary data with optional semantic tags. Async remains a direct dashed data edge. Clock/Trigger is a visible source. Derived statecharts are out, and behavior-tree work is deferred to its own later research. Track B now inventories the full off-canvas editor surface rather than only per-Block controls.

Track A · node and block vocabulary

Concepts pyblocks might render as a Block, region, port, source, or cable when the source really carries that shape. Entries are organized by concept, not vendor.

Concept and readingEvidence and SystemSketch projection
Already have
A-HAVE · 01

Exclusive branch / case / φ join

Python if and match already read as an exclusive Branch region with a join. LabVIEW Case, Blueprint Branch/Switch, and Simulink If/Merge confirm the settled reading grammar; they do not justify a new palette node.

Primary documentation: NI Case Structures · Epic Flow Control · MathWorks If

Existing SystemSketch UI
Already have
A-HAVE · 02

Loop-carried previous value / delayed edge

A loop-carried value already has a distinct z⁻¹ treatment, separating a prior iteration from same-iteration data. LabVIEW Feedback and Simulink Unit Delay corroborate that reading while their simulation-time rules remain outside ordinary Python.

Primary documentation: NI Feedback Node · MathWorks Unit Delay

Existing SystemSketch UI
Already have
A-HAVE · 03

Named record-field projection / Split

The stock Split preset already projects a resolved record into name-stable accessor rows. This is SystemSketch's existing equivalent of Unbundle By Name, Split Struct Pin, and Bus Selector; the earlier report incorrectly called it missing.

Primary documentation: NI Unbundle By Name · Epic Struct Variables · MathWorks Bus Selector

Existing SystemSketch UI
Already have
A-HAVE · 04

Ordinary data paths for event, error, state, and configuration values

These meanings do not require another transport. A typed value can already travel through an ordinary arrow or tunnel to a handler, bus, or component; the missing improvement is a semantic role label on that same path, not a new event dispatcher or exception rail.

Primary documentation: NI Handling Errors · MathWorks Signal Types

Existing SystemSketch UI
Already have
A-HAVE · 05

Normal return versus derived mutation effect

A port declared mutating already derives a top-edge effect exit, preventing an in-place-looking write from reading like an ordinary returned value. This borrows the reader benefit of Blueprint pure/impure distinction without importing pervasive execution cables.

Primary documentation: Epic Functions

Named partial record update / Set attributes

Bundle By Name, Set Members in Struct, and Bus Assignment converge on the same readable operation: update selected named members while preserving the rest. Zach has approved shipping the already-designed batched setattr shape as a stock Block with ordinary record data in and out.

Primary documentation: NI Bundle By Name · Epic Struct Variables · MathWorks Bus Assignment

Official reference UI

Lift · medium. The drawing and source intent already exist. Shipping still needs a stock preset, named-row editing, source-projection rules, and regression coverage for batched writes and preserved members.

Missing, would be useful
A-USEFUL · 02

Conditional value selection / Select

LabVIEW Select and Simulink Switch make a value choice distinct from an effectful branch. Epic's RigVM API documents the same Condition / If True / If False contract, but its reference page does not publish a graph screenshot, so this row does not substitute a documentation table for actual tool UI. Zach has approved a stock Select Block for Python's true_value if condition else false_value: two value inputs, one Boolean control value, and one ordinary output.

Primary documentation: NI Select · Epic Make Select · MathWorks Switch

Official reference UI

Lift · low to medium. Add the stock preset and source projection, keep its output on the data plane, and test that it remains visually and semantically distinct from the Branch region.

Missing, would be useful
A-USEFUL · 03

Analyzer-recognised asynchronous data path

LabVIEW's asynchronous channel wire and Simulink's dash-dot function-call control signals show that delivery semantics can deserve a redundant cable cue. In SystemSketch this remains a direct data path: use the existing dashed async edge only when source proves asynchronous delivery, with no invented queue box, junction, or ownership topology. In the MathWorks example E1/E2 are periodic function-call controls and E3 is interrupt-driven—not generic asynchronous payload cables.

Primary documentation: NI Using Wires · MathWorks Model Reference Function-Call · MathWorks Signal Types

Official reference UI

Lift · medium to high. The cable style already ships. The real work is a conservative source fact for async delivery and an inspector explanation that does not claim buffering, ordering, or queue ownership.

Missing, would be useful
A-USEFUL · 04

Clock / Trigger stock source

A visible Clock or Trigger source makes a real periodic or external activation legible without hiding scheduling inside a downstream Block. It emits an ordinary typed trigger/event/control value; the rate or source is explicit, and adapters may map that value to Python, ROS, or event-loop timing.

Primary documentation: NI Timing and Synchronization · MathWorks Function-Call Generator · MathWorks Model Reference Function-Call

Official reference UI

Lift · medium. Define a stock source, rate/source fields, and explicit runtime-adapter contract. It must never imply that merely drawing a 10 Hz block creates a hidden scheduler.

Missing, would not be useful

Text only by design: these would add palette or host-runtime semantics, not reveal Python.

Concept and readingEvidence and SystemSketch projection
Missing, would not be useful

Explicit exception / Cast Failed / railway outcome rail

Exceptions, narrowing failures such as Blueprint Cast Failed, and railway-style outcomes are normal data in SystemSketch. Route an Error-tagged value through ordinary arrows or tunnels to a shared handler or bus; do not reuse the top-edge mutation-effect grammar or put a special failure pin on every call.

Primary documentation: NI Handling Errors · Epic Cast To

Missing, would not be useful

Bespoke event-dispatch relation

An event is a value—often a record with type, time, payload, or timeout—and follows normal dataflow. A preset Event tag can explain its role without adding registration cables, dispatcher nodes, or a second execution model.

Primary documentation: NI Event Structure · Epic Bind and Unbind Events · MathWorks Stateflow Events

Missing, would not be useful

Derived state-machine or statechart overlay

State/configuration values and their real dataflow already express the useful model. Do not derive a separate statechart from ordinary enum-and-conditional code; Stateflow remains reference evidence, not a requested SystemSketch layer.

Primary documentation: MathWorks Stateflow States

Missing, would not be useful

Arithmetic, comparisons, collections, and signal-routing palettes

LabVIEW numeric/Boolean, Blueprint Array/Map/Set, and Simulink math/routing palettes are authoring conveniences. Python already states operators, calls, unpacking, indexing, and collection construction; special glyph libraries would add a second language rather than a renderer fact.

Primary documentation: NI Block Diagram Explained · Epic Blueprint Palette · MathWorks Library Browser

Missing, would not be useful

Implicit Sequence, Gate, DoOnce, Delay, and scheduler controls

These encode tool-specific pulses, latches, wall-clock policy, or simulator scheduling without a source-owned value. Preserve explicit Python order. This exclusion does not apply to the proposed visible Clock/Trigger source above.

Primary documentation: Epic Flow Control

Missing, would not be useful

Formula/MATLAB Function, macros, and authorable interface subgraphs

These are text escape hatches or reusable graph-authoring systems in palette tools. SystemSketch already takes the stronger source-first position: Python is canonical and linked definitions are the presentation seam.

Primary documentation: MathWorks MATLAB Function · Epic Blueprint Macros

Missing, would not be useful

Property/Invoke, variants, construction/spawn, hardware, and runtime palettes

Framework APIs, Unreal lifecycle nodes, LabVIEW hardware controls, and Simulink time/sample-rate configuration belong to their host runtimes. They are ordinary Python calls or deliberately outside a static Python renderer.

Primary documentation: Epic Blueprint Class UI · NI Block Diagram Explained · MathWorks Simulink Editor

Missing, would not be useful

State history junctions and visual variant pickers

History restoration and variant activation have specialised runtime contracts but no dependable generic Python syntax. Do not infer hidden statechart memory or add a canvas-side configuration picker.

Synthesis

Your thinking, sharpened

These are scoped inferences from primary documentation and the live tree—not claims that the three reference tools share one execution model.

1 · Split was already the answer.

The stock Split preset and its named accessor rows already implement the useful Unbundle By Name / Split Struct / Bus Selector reading.

2 · Set attributes is the missing twin.

The designed batched named update should ship as a stock Block with ordinary record data in/out; mutation metadata remains separate.

3 · Select is data, not execution.

Two candidate values plus one Boolean control value map cleanly to Python's conditional expression and one ordinary output.

4 · Event and error are roles, not transports.

Data/Event/Configuration/State/Control/Error tags explain ordinary ports and arrows. No dispatcher cable, exception rail, or top-edge side effect is needed.

5 · The Simulink E-lines are control events.

E1/E2 schedule periodic function calls and E3 is interrupt-driven; their dash-dot style supports a redundant semantic cue, not a generic async-queue claim.

6 · Clock/Trigger must be explicit.

A visible source can emit ticks as typed data. It must name its rate/adapter and never hide a scheduler in the drawing.

7 · Off-canvas convergence is mostly already present.

SystemSketch already has the menu, command search, library, Inspector, Problems, overview, depth, comments, zoom, and contextual layout core.

8 · The best chrome gaps are semantic.

Source provenance, definition/reference navigation, source-linked diagnostics, landmarks, cable hierarchy, interface tracing, and a board-wide fact table reveal identity the current generic panes cannot.

9 · Play controls need a real authority.

Run/Pause/Stop is worth designing only around an explicit target adapter; trace playback and probes must be transient evidence, never board state.

Decision surface

Done / left / needs Zach / deliberately not done

This remains research: it records approved directions and decision surfaces but makes no hidden product, schema, analyzer, or runtime change.

Done

  • Reclassified Split, defaults/overrides, and variadics from missing to shipped.
  • Ran independent LabVIEW, Blueprint, and Simulink application-chrome passes.
  • Added every current major menu/panel seam and the useful semantic gaps.
  • Embedded 39 unique official-reference screenshots.

Left

  • Ship approved Set attributes and Select stock Blocks.
  • Design Clock/Trigger source facts and enable semantic tag presets.
  • Prototype Source lens, source-linked Problems, semantic search, landmarks, and the board-wide fact table.
  • Define a runtime/trace adapter contract before any play controls.

Needs Zach

  • Should the right surfaces become explicit tabs?
  • Should source/project navigation begin at one board or the whole workspace?
  • Do Run controls belong now, or should imported trace playback come first?
  • Should semantic tags be analyzer-only, user-chosen presentation, or both with provenance?

Deliberately not done

  • No bespoke event/error transport or derived statechart.
  • No vendor node palette, ribbon, schema editor, mask system, or mutable project manager.
  • No inert Compile/Play buttons, solver UI, deployment settings, or fake live debugger.
  • Behavior trees remain a separate later research track.
